headline: Prosecutors used ChatGPT logs as evidence in deadly Palisades fire trial, jury deadlocked
summary: Prosecutors presented ChatGPT logs as evidence in an arson trial, but the jury remained unconvinced, resulting in a hung jury and a mistrial.
details: Jonathan Rinderknecht faced arson charges for a New Year's Day 2025 fire, one of LA's deadliest wildfires. Prosecutors built their case using location data, security camera footage, witness testimony, and his ChatGPT logs.

The prosecution highlighted Rinderknecht's ChatGPT activity, which included generating fire images, asking "Why am I so angry all the time?", and ranting about the wealthy. A screen recording also showed him asking the chatbot if someone could be blamed for a fire started by their cigarette.
Despite this evidence, the jurors were not convinced. The trial concluded in a deadlock with a 10-2 vote in favor of the defense, prompting the judge to declare a hung jury and a mistrial.

One juror told CBS LA that she didn't consider the ChatGPT logs as proof, stating, "I talk to ChatGPT all the time." She expressed anger at the suggestion that his chatbot use indicated a character flaw.

headline_marked: [[Micron briefly surpasses Meta, Tesla]] in market cap, stock up 236% in a month
headline: Micron briefly surpasses Meta, Tesla in market cap, stock up 236% in a month
summary: Memory chip maker Micron saw its market valuation briefly exceed Meta and Tesla, driven by soaring demand for AI-specific memory. Its stock has surged over 236% in the past month.
details: Micron, the memory chip maker, briefly surpassed Meta and Tesla in market valuation on Thursday, closing Friday with a market cap near $1.27 trillion. Its stock has soared over 236% in the past month alone, reaching $1,132 a share.

This dizzying rise is fueled by the AI data center buildout boom, creating a shortage of system memory chips like DRAM and NAND, particularly High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM). A single AI server demands significantly more memory than a standard laptop.

AI system makers like Nvidia and hyperscalers such as Microsoft, Amazon AWS, Google, Meta, and Oracle are buying vast quantities of memory. This "RAMageddon" is predicted to persist into 2027, driving up prices for consumer electronics.

Micron reported blockbuster third-quarter earnings, with revenue quadrupling year-over-year to $41.45 billion and profits skyrocketing to $28.2 billion. The company also provided a strong Q4 outlook, forecasting $49 billion to $51 billion in revenue.

To counter historical bust cycles, Micron has secured long-term supply agreements with key customers, including Nvidia and AI lab Anthropic. These 16 strategic customer agreements across data center, consumer, and auto markets aim to transform its business model.

Analysts are optimistic, with William Blair's Sebastien Naji noting that demand growth continues to outpace new cleanroom space. This potential for more durable earnings growth has led to reiterated "Outperform" ratings for Micron.
